advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether _validate_authorized_delta should compare only stable identity fields (id, author, normalized_body) rather than full raw comment dicts to avoid aborting mid-DELETE on benign non-target metadata drift.
evidence: `if manifest_tools._canonical(observed) != manifest_tools._canonical(expected): raise CleanupError("live Jira comments drifted outside authorized deletions")`
`normalized_comment = copy.deepcopy(comment)` in comment_echo_reclaim_manifest.py:397 — the observed comment retains all raw Jira page fields incl. volatile `updated`/rendered content
advisory.finding: _validate_authorized_delta compares the full canonical Jira inventory (deep-copied raw comment dicts including mutable fields like `updated`, rendered bodies, `self`) between the frozen jira-before.json and each live re-capture; any benign edit to a NON-target comment on the three issues between freeze and execution triggers 'live Jira comments drifted outside authorized deletions' and aborts mid-cleanup.
scenarios: An operator or another integration edits/updates an unrelated comment on REB-1567/REB-1931/REB-2605 during the quiet window

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test seeding a journal that ends on a bare `delete_intent` while the target comment is still present, and assert the resume re-attempts the DELETE without advancing the completed count.
evidence: cleanup.py:510-525 `if progress == "unresolved": ... target_present = _target_present(observation, action); recovered_count = completed_count if target_present else completed_count + 1`

test class CrashAfterDeleteJira delete_comment: `status = super().delete_comment(...)` runs (removes comment) THEN `raise SimulatedCrash` — target is absent, so only the `target_present=False` path is covered
ABSENCE: no test constructs a journal ending in a lone delete_intent with the deletion target still present in the live inventory
advisory.finding: The cleanup resume `unresolved` branch with the target still present is untested: no test seeds a journal that ends on a bare `delete_intent` (crash between intent-append and outcome-append) while the delete never reached Jira, so the sub-branch that keeps `recovered_count = completed_count` (does NOT advance), journals `recovered`/`target_present`, and re-attempts the DELETE is never exercised. All crash tests (`CrashAfterDeleteJira`) call `super().delete_comment` (removing the comment) before raising, so `target_present` is always False there.
scenarios: Operator process is killed after fsyncing the delete intent but before the DELETE request reaches Jira; on resume the tool must not count that action as completed and must retry the DELETE.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a fake transport / prewritten journal that leaves exactly one trailing delete_intent record with the target comment still in the inventory, run execute, and assert delete_calls includes a retry for that target and the journal gains a recovered/target_present outcome then a successful outcome.

ABSENCE: search for `previous Jira cleanup postcondition failed` / resume-after-postcondition_failed test returned no matches
advisory.finding: The `postcondition_failed` resume path is untested: `_outcome_state` raises `CleanupError('previous Jira cleanup postcondition failed')` when a resumed journal's last outcome record has `delete_result == 'postcondition_failed'`, but no test re-runs the tool against a journal already ending in that outcome. `test_canary_stops_before_second_delete_when_any_non_target_comment_drifts` writes the postcondition_failed record but never resumes from it (the raise it asserts originates from `_validate_authorized_delta` in the same run, not from `_outcome_state` on a subsequent run).
scenarios: An operator re-runs the digest-confirmed command after a run that recorded a postcondition_failed outcome; the tool must refuse rather than proceed.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the drift test produces the postcondition_failed journal, re-run cleanup.run with the same artifacts and a fresh FakeJira and assert it raises the 'previous Jira cleanup postcondition failed' CleanupError and issues no new delete_calls.
